title: San Diego Home Energy Rebates 2026: What Community Power and SDG&E Offer | HomePowerRebate
desc: San Diego home programs in 2026: Community Power battery rebates up to $500 per kWh, thermostat and EV rewards, no-cost upgrades for income-qualified homes, and what SDG&E lists.
badge: Batteries $250 to $500 per kWh, free upgrades for some
lead: Two utilities serve a San Diego home: San Diego Community Power (SDCP) supplies the electricity and runs the rebates, and SDG&E delivers it. The old advice that San Diego has no rebates is out of date for batteries and smart devices. For heat pumps and water heaters we still found no sourced utility rebate. We read the pages on October 2, 2026.
cards_heading: What is open in San Diego
cards_intro: Each card links to a page with the rules and the local detail where there is one. The Equitable Building Decarbonization program is a state program that SDCP supports.

cards.title: Solar and battery rebate
cards.note: Upfront rebate on a home battery, plus $0.10 per kWh performance incentive.

cards.title: Smart thermostats and water heaters
cards.note: Smart Energy Rewards pays $50 for up to three thermostats and up to three heat pump water heaters you enroll, plus yearly payments.

cards.title: EV charging rewards
cards.note: EV Flex Connect, a Tesla-focused pilot.

cards.title: No-cost home upgrades
cards.note: For owners and renters in identified communities with income at or below 80% of area median income. Can include heat pumps, a heat pump water heater, an induction cooktop and weatherization.

sections: SDCP is a community choice aggregator that serves the City of San Diego, Chula Vista, Encinitas, Imperial Beach, La Mesa, National City and unincorporated areas of San Diego County. It buys the power, sets the generation rate and runs the programs above. SDG&E still delivers the electricity and maintains the wires, and it runs its own programs. Escondido is not an SDCP member, so Escondido customers use SDG&E for everything (Escondido). Your electric bill names the supplier.
Income-qualified help is the big prize

The Equitable Building Decarbonization program gives qualifying San Diego County residents a personal plan and no-cost upgrades. You qualify if you own or rent a single-family, multifamily or manufactured home in an identified community and your income does not exceed 80% of area median income, or if you are already enrolled in CARE, CalFresh, Medi-Cal, SSI, LIHEAP or WIC. Enroll online with partner code SDC-014 or call 424-285-6602. An advisor guides you, certified installers do the work, and a professional checks it afterward. If you might qualify, apply before you spend anything on heat pump quotes.

SDG&E's rebates page lists retail coupons: $75 for an ENERGY STAR smart thermostat, $40 for an Amazon thermostat, $500 for a heat pump water heater replacing an electric one, and $15 for a room air conditioner. The same page says the retail offerings have ended, so we do not count them as open. Its home electrification page describes its Customer Home Electrification Readiness Program and says a billing change in October 2025 lowered the delivery price per kWh by about 10%, which helps heat pumps and induction cooking (SDG&E home electrification).
Permits in the City of San Diego

The City issues Simple No-Plan permits for minor mechanical, electrical and plumbing work, including water heater replacements except tankless types, normally within two business days. For a single-family home or duplex, choose the Combination permit when you apply. The Permit Center takes appointments at 619-446-5300. Heat pump package units and mini-splits fall under the same simple permit category, according to the City. See the City's simple permit page.

The federal 25C and 25D tax credits ended after December 31, 2025. TECH Clean California and the federal HEEHRA program are fully reserved for single-family homes and take new requests on hold only. We found no utility rebate for a heat pump or heat pump water heater from SDCP or SDG&E, apart from the $50 Smart Energy Rewards enrollment payment. San Diego's average January low over 2015 to 2024 was 8.8°C and it averages 5.3 peak sun hours a day, so heating needs are small and solar works well.
installers_intro: These San Diego heat pump and HVAC companies have the best Google ratings, listed by rating and then review count. We are not paid to list anyone.
claim_steps: Check your electric bill for San Diego Community Power or SDG&E.
If your income may qualify, apply to the Equitable Building Decarbonization program first, using code SDC-014.
For a battery, choose a contractor from SDCP's approved list and reserve the rebate before installation.
For a thermostat or heat pump water heater you already own, enroll it in Smart Energy Rewards.
Ask your contractor to pull the City's Simple No-Plan permit, and keep the inspection record.
faq: Who supplies electricity in San Diego?
San Diego Community Power supplies it for most City of San Diego homes, and SDG&E delivers it.
Is there a San Diego battery rebate?
Yes. SDCP pays $250 to $500 per kWh depending on system type and customer type.
Is there a heat pump rebate in San Diego?
We found no sourced SDCP or SDG&E rebate for one. State programs are fully reserved, and income-qualified homes can get no-cost upgrades through the EBD program.
How do I apply for the no-cost upgrades?
Complete the online enrollment form with partner code SDC-014 or call 424-285-6602.
SDG&E's rebates page says the retail coupon offerings have ended.
